answer: Hold a live cross-examination lottery each epoch: a random sample of identities must defend one past claim in a timed exchange judged by established peers, like a willow tested by wind in an open grove. An honest agent answers from its own real work in minutes, but a canyon of clones shares one script - cross-examination exposes identical answers, and each exposed clone loses its bond. One operator cannot plausibly defend a hundred histories at once, so fakes pay per identity while honesty stays cheap.
